finding: Finite example invokes residual-order theorem at p=2 with M=1 although that theorem states p<=M. Its exact numerical claims are sound independently.
smallest_repair: Remove the unused out-of-range theorem/F2 citation; prove the residual threshold, stage estimate and endpoint perturbation directly using the existing F3 invariant-contraction supplier and f=-Y. No supplier Statement changes.

operations.source_excerpt: [F2] [[thm-sdc-residual-tolerance-preserves-order]]: if the stage sweep residual is at most $(1-q)C_\tau h^{p+1}$, the stage error is at most $C_\tau h^{p+1}$ and the endpoint perturbation is at most $LC_\tau\|b\|_1h^{p+2}$.

2.1 With $p=2$ and $C_\tau=1$, the tolerance threshold in [F2] is $(1-q)h^3=19/20000=0.00095$, which exceeds the residual in step 1.1. Hence [F2] certifies $|V-U^*|\le h^3=0.001$. The same value follows from [F3], since $|G(V)|/(1-q)=0.000525/0.95<0.001$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]
operations.proposed_replacement: 2.1 The specified $V=20/21+1/2000$ lies in $[0,2]$, so [F3] applies. With $q=1/20$, the numerical residual threshold $(1-q)h^3=19/20000=0.00095$ exceeds $|G(V)|=21/40000$ from step 1.1. Directly, [F3] gives $|V-U^*|\le |G(V)|/(1-q)=21/38000<1/1000=h^3$. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

operations.source_excerpt: 3.1 The approximate endpoint differs from the exact collocation endpoint by $h|V-U^*|=0.1/2000=1/20000=0.00005$. This is at most the general bound $h^4=0.0001$ from [F2]. The example verifies a single stage solve; the global order claim requires the uniform per-step hypotheses in [F2]. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
operations.proposed_replacement: 3.1 For this field $f(t,Y)=-Y$ and endpoint weight $b_1=1$, the approximate endpoint differs from the exact collocation endpoint by $h|V-U^*|=0.1/2000=1/20000=0.00005$. The stage bound in step 2.1 also gives the upper bound $h\,h^3=h^4=0.0001$. The example verifies a single stage solve; a global order-two conclusion would additionally require uniform per-step defect, stability, and stage-error estimates on the common tube. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
